definition: A physically accurate run has a pose between Up and the next Contact where both feet are off the ground (the flight phase), but a common stylized/anime (sakuga) convention deliberately skips drawing it, cutting directly from the Up pose to the following Contact - a named, deliberate stylistic economy choice, not a physical error.
purpose: Qualify continuous_ground_contact_except_during_flight_phase's physical rule with a real, named style exception: the physically-real flight-phase pose is often intentionally omitted in stylized 2D convention, which a naive 'the flight phase must be keyed' check would wrongly flag as missing.
visible_effect: A run cycle that cuts straight from the Up pose to the next Contact, with no intermediate both-feet-off-the-ground drawing, still reads clearly as a run in the sakuga convention the source studies - the omission is not perceived as an error by the convention's own audience.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: Skipping the flight-phase pose is an economy-of-drawings choice (one fewer key per cycle) that this source treats as a legitimate, common stylistic decision rather than a corner cut carelessly.
physical_interpretation: The flight phase is still physically real even when its drawing is omitted - the omission is a representational choice (which poses get drawn), not a claim that the physical event does not happen.
use_cases: deciding whether a stylized run cycle needs an explicit flight-phase key, or can cut directly from Up to the next Contact as a deliberate stylistic economy
reviewing a stylized or anime-influenced run cycle against continuous_ground_contact_except_during_flight_phase's physical rule without over-flagging a legitimate stylistic omission as a defect
non_use_cases: a realistic or simulation-driven run, where the source's own framing implies the flight-phase pose is expected, not optional
a walk cycle, where no flight phase exists to omit in the first place
interactions: continuous_ground_contact_except_during_flight_phase (W03, video 26) - this entry is the direct style-level qualifier for that entry's physical rule: the flight phase is still real, but a stylized convention may not draw or key it explicitly
ai/style.js - a natural place a declared style ('sakuga-influenced', 'anime') could record 'flight-phase pose typically omitted' as a per-style convention, once such conventions are authored

style_variations.sakuga_anime: flight-phase pose typically omitted; cuts directly from Up to the next Contact

cadence_representation: Not computed. Nothing in ai/style.js currently records this or any per-style convention about which physically-real poses a style typically omits; continuous_ground_contact_except_during_flight_phase's check (once built) would need this exception registered against a declared style, or it would incorrectly flag every sakuga-convention run cycle as missing its flight phase.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Not applicable directly - this is a qualifier on a check (continuous_ground_contact_except_during_flight_phase) that is itself not yet built, rather than a new measurement of its own.
failure_modes: flagging a stylized run cycle's omitted flight-phase pose as an error, when it is a deliberate and common convention in the style being emulated
conversely, omitting the flight-phase pose in a REALISTIC run where the source's framing implies it should be present
roblox_considerations: None beyond the shared keyframe model.
performance_implications: Omitting a key is a minor authoring-cost saving, not a runtime concern.
examples: "in real life there's actually a pose between the up and contact where both feet are off the ground, but I noticed that in a lot of sakuga animation they tended to just skip this over and go directly from the up pose to the following contact" - video @ 03:10-03:25

confirmed again in a second, independent sakuga study even under extreme perspective distortion: "even though she's right up in the camera, they're still keeping that contact down up pose" [sequence, with no separate flight-phase drawing] - video @ 09:59-10:04
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/nKvBYXzRszw @ 03:10-03:25 and @ 09:59-10:04 - stated directly by the presenter (moderndayjames) while breaking down real professional sakuga run cycles frame by frame, the second passage independently confirming the same convention in a different (Kill la Kill) source; experimental until validated
